# OTITIS MEDIA

Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenza are the most common pathogens that cause otitis media. Group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Moraxella catarrhalis are less frequent causes.

---

References:

- Harmes et al, American Family Physician. 2013, 88(7)435-440
- Mandell chapter: Otitis Externa, Otitis Media, and Mastoiditis
- Sanford keyword: Otitis media
- Up-to-Date Online: Acute otitis media in adults
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Preferred treatment

Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [R]

### Alternatives

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [R]
Secondary alternatives, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:
Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [DI]
< OR >
Cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID for 10 days ($$) [R]

## Outpatient

### Preferred treatment

Patient has NOT received antibiotics in the prior month:
Amoxicillin 1000 mg PO q8h for 10 days ($) [R]

Patient has received antibiotics in the prior month:
Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [R]

### Preferred Alternative

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [R]
< OR >
Azithromycin 500 mg PO once on day 1, then 250 mg PO q24h for 4 days ($) [O]

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Outpatient):*
Secondary alternatives, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:
Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 10 days ($) [DI]
